newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian private sector grows modestly in Jan-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Romanian private sector grows modestly in Jan-Sept.

text.p: The Romanian private sector's share of the economy showed modest growth in the nine months to end-September, according to National Statistics Board data.
Local analysts said expensive banking credits and high taxes were behind the mediocre evolution of the private sector in the first three quarters of the year.
The private sector's share of nine-month exports amounting to $5.45 billion rose slightly to 43.8 percent from 40.8 percent in the equivalent period of 1995, statistics showed.

Its share of January-September retail sales, put at a total 15.67 trillion lei, was also modest -- 79 percent versus 75.5 percent last year -- while its contribution to commercial services provided to the population showed an insignificant rise -- 73 percent from 72.2.
"It's rather difficult to go ahead in private enterprises when profit taxes are so high," said a local economist.
Romania charges a profit tax of 38 percent.
"The access to banking credits is prohibitive and high rates...render wide-scope investment almost impossible," the daily newspaper Curierul National said on Wednesday.
Lending rates now stand at an average 55 percent.
High taxes and discouraging lending rates, as well as lower purchasing power, push many smaller entrepreneurs into closing down their businesses, the newspaper said.

The private sector, almost non-existent before communists were ousted in 1989, is expected to take up to 60 percent of Romania's gross domestic product this year, up from 45 percent in 1995. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
